review.source: PHEBS-46 keeps phebs.thrift.caller.go bound to thrift-contract@1.1.2 plus thrift-caller@1.6.0-released.1 and moves its claim to 1.1.0. The resolver catalog (pack 1.4.0, policy thriftrw-yarpc-module-package-sha1-v1) relates a thriftrw-plugin-yarpc client to a .thrift declaration only when the one thriftrw package its Helper.Args calls go through, located through the repository's go.mod modules, embeds ThriftModule{Package: that import path, FilePath, SHA1} and exactly one declared .thrift file at FilePath has that content SHA-1. The admission matrix is unchanged and re-run.
review.evidence: With no generated-from snapshot, a YARPC client modelled on yarpc-go output resolves callers held from echoclient.New(...) and as an echoclient.Interface value, end to end through materialization, publication and the direct-syntax scan, with the Thrift method spelling (Go PingTwice is ping_twice). A hash mismatch and an ambiguous match are explicit abstentions; a client without a module is not described; an explicit generated-from mapping governs. A mutation dropping the SHA-1 comparison fails these tests. The describer, run once over all 19 real yarpc-go clients at 7000bc61, described 15 (49 symbols); the other 4 are empty or extends-only services.
review.security: Existing authenticated visibility/source/generation/citation fences, signed binary/artifact bindings and identity checks retained. The relation is verified by content hash; nothing is inferred from directory names.
review.steady_state_cost: At catalog build only: one bounded read per .go file named client.go in a directory ending in client, one parse per referenced thriftrw module file and one content read per candidate .thrift file, within the existing blob read and byte budgets, plus a 4,096-client bound. The resolver pack bump re-materializes each catalog once. Nothing per query or sync tick.
